content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement satisfies the MINCOMMIT preferred position (not merely the fallback): fees run to usage or ordered services only, with no minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap binding Corio.

Key support:
- **Revenue share is purely variable** (p0157–p0160): a percentage of Application Management Revenue actually invoiced, excluding professional services and network access fees, accruing only once a Corio Customer goes live.
- **Implementation fees** are time-and-materials against an agreed SOW with a stated cap (p0161), and are invoiced only after successful milestone completion (p0167) — ordered services, not a commitment.
- **Volume is uncapped, not committed**: "SOFTWARE USERS: BuySite Hosted Edition: Unlimited" (p0151), unlimited Customer sublicensing (p0032), unlimited MarketSite.net access (p0041).
- **Maintenance is economically elective**: it continues only "provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees" (p0055, p0098), so we can walk away from that spend.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged:
- The five-year initial term with no convenience-termination right (p0096) carries annual MarketSite.net access and maintenance fees, but those buy unlimited-access service actually made available — a subscription for services received, not a committed minimum volume, so the multi-year take-or-pay walk-away trigger isn't met.
- The "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" (p0158) is the only "minimum" hit in the document, and it is a threshold on a fee *waiver* that benefits us (the 3000 royalty-free licenses) — not a purchase obligation, so flagging it would work against our side.
- Exhibit D's initial-customer and marketing items are expressly "non-binding" (p0198) and efforts-based (p0205), creating no quota.

Per the classification rules, a clause meeting the preferred position is not redlined, so I made no edits and submitted a single compliant finding.
